```{r setup}
library(httr2)
library(dplyr)
library(purrr)
library(readr)
library(tibble)
library(stringr)
library(jsonlite)

`%||%` <- function(a, b) if (is.null(a) || length(a) == 0) b else a
key <- Sys.getenv("GOVINFO_API_KEY")

private_dir <- "govinfo_private"
dir.create(private_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
```

Test the API connection without printing the key:

```{r test-api}
collections <- request("https://api.govinfo.gov/collections") |>
  req_url_query(api_key = key) |>
  req_perform() |>
  resp_body_json(simplifyVector = FALSE)
cat("GovInfo collections endpoint responded successfully.\n")
```

## 2. GovInfo API Search

The API search uses the query pattern provided in the assignment. Check the returned titles/metadata to ensure that the documents actually belong to the Senate Committee on Foreign Relations (not the House Committee on Foreign Affairs).

```{r api-search}
body <- list( query = 'collection:(CHRG) AND "Committee on Foreign Relations"',
              pageSize = 100,  offsetMark = "*", sorts = list(list(field = "publishdate", sortOrder = "DESC")))

found <- request("https://api.govinfo.gov/search") |>
  req_url_query(api_key = key) |>
  req_body_json(body) |>
  req_perform() |>
  resp_body_json(simplifyVector = FALSE)


if (is.null(found$results)) {stop("No `results` field found. Inspect names(found) and GovInfo API docs.")}

results_tbl <- purrr::map_dfr(found$results, function(x) {
  tibble(packageId = as.character(x$packageId %||% NA_character_),
         title = as.character(x$title %||% NA_character_),
         dateIssued = as.character(x$dateIssued %||% NA_character_),
         lastModified = as.character(x$lastModified %||% NA_character_))})

head(results_tbl, 10)
```

### 2.1 Select and Verify Ten Hearings

Review the API results and confirm that each selected hearing is a **Senate Foreign Relations Committee** hearing. A keyword match alone can include unrelated records. If fewer than ten eligible records appear, retrieve further pages using the returned `offsetMark` as described in the assignment.

```{r select-ten}
if (nrow(results_tbl) < 10) stop("Fewer than 10 search results; use API paging.")
selected <- results_tbl |> slice_head(n = 10)
print(selected)
```

## 3. Download Ten PDFs and Keep a Log

The GovInfo packages endpoint provides document metadata and links to PDF and other formats. Downloads are saved in a private folder, not the published website.

```{r download-pdfs}
#| label: download-pdfs

get_package_summary <- function(id) {
  request(paste0(
    "https://api.govinfo.gov/packages/",
    id, "/summary"
  )) |>
    req_url_query(api_key = key) |>
    req_perform() |>
    resp_body_json(simplifyVector = FALSE)
}

summaries <- purrr::map(
  selected$packageId,
  get_package_summary
)

get_pdf_url <- function(s, id) {

  api_url <- s$download$pdfLink

  if (!is.null(api_url) &&
      is.character(api_url) &&
      length(api_url) == 1 &&
      !is.na(api_url) &&
      grepl("^https://", api_url)) {
    return(api_url)
  }

  paste0("https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/",id, "/pdf/", id, ".pdf")
}

pdf_urls <- purrr::map2_chr(summaries, selected$packageId, get_pdf_url)

print(tibble( packageId = selected$packageId, pdf_url = pdf_urls))

dir.create(private_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

safe_id <- gsub("[^A-Za-z0-9_-]",  "_",  selected$packageId)

log_tbl <- purrr::map_dfr(seq_len(nrow(selected)), function(i) {
  destination <- file.path(private_dir, paste0(safe_id[i], ".pdf"))

  status <- tryCatch({

    download.file(pdf_urls[i], destfile = destination, mode = "wb", quiet = TRUE)

    if (!file.exists(destination) ||
        file.size(destination) < 5) {
      stop("File missing or empty")
    }

    con <- file(destination, open = "rb")
    signature <- tryCatch(readBin(con, what = "raw", n = 5), finally = close(con))

    if (!identical(
      signature,
      charToRaw("%PDF-")
    )) {
      stop("Downloaded file is not a PDF")
    }
    "success"}, error = function(e) {
    if (file.exists(destination)) {unlink(destination)}
    paste("failed:", conditionMessage(e))})

  Sys.sleep(1)

  tibble(
    packageId = selected$packageId[i],
    title = selected$title[i],
    pdf_file = basename(destination),
    pdf_url = pdf_urls[i],
    status = status,
    downloaded_at = as.character(Sys.time())
  )
})

write_csv(log_tbl,"assign05_download_log.csv")

print(log_tbl)

cat("\nSuccessful downloads:", sum(log_tbl$status == "success"), "out of", nrow(log_tbl), "\n")
```

### 3.1 Compare the API and Website Export

Compare the ten API `packageId` values against the manually exported CSV/JSON list. Note any difference in query filtering, date sorting, or publication updates. **Do not claim the lists match until you have checked.**

```{r compare-manual}
manual <- readr::read_csv("data/assign05_download_log.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)

print(names(manual))
print(nrow(manual))

manual <- manual |>
  dplyr::filter(trimws(collection) == "Congressional Hearings",!is.na(packageId))

comparison <- selected |>
  dplyr::mutate(in_website_export = trimws(packageId) %in% trimws(manual$packageId)) |>
  dplyr::select(packageId, title, in_website_export)

print(comparison)

cat("Matched hearings:", sum(comparison$in_website_export), "out of", nrow(comparison), "\n")
```

All ten hearings identified through the GovInfo API were also found in the manually exported website results based on their package IDs. Both searches used the same query and were sorted by publication date from newest to oldest. No differences were found among the ten selected hearings, indicating consistent results between the API and website searches for these records.

## 4. Short Report

### 4.1 Usability of PDF Documents as Data

The hearing PDFs contain useful information, but they are not easy to use directly for data analysis. To analyze them, I would need to extract the text, organize the information, and check for errors. Scanned PDFs may also require OCR.

### 4.2 Improvements Using Other Formats and Metadata

The GovInfo API provided information such as package IDs, titles, and publication dates. The package summaries did not include direct PDF links for the selected hearings, but I was able to download all ten PDFs using the standard GovInfo URLs. Other formats, such as XML or text, could make the data easier to process.

### 4.3 What Did the API Provide?

The API made it possible to search for hearings and download documents using R. Compared with searching the website manually or scraping webpages, it was easier to repeat the process and keep track of the results.
